cases.why: I verified against Chrome's own AX tree that the print button's computed accessible name is 'inkjet printer' — the visible 'Print' caption is `aria-hidden="true"` and contributes nothing. So the image IS the control's sole name, and it names the depicted device rather than the action, failing Understanding 1.1.1 Situation B and F30 ('the text … cannot be used in place of the non-text content without losing information or function'). The two sibling buttons ARE correctly purpose-named ('Add to Apple Wallet', 'Email boarding pass') and the judge praised them for exactly that — so the rubric holds the right concept and applied the wrong test here. The rubric even carries the correct clause (alt-text-adequacy-v0.md:50-58), but its escape hatch — 'if the enclosing link/button ALREADY has its own accessible name … the icon is not the control's name' — has NO backing signal: nothing computes or ships the enclosing control's accessible name. What the judge does get is a screenshot in which a 'Print' caption is plainly visible, which fires the hatch. (Contributing: the measured `nearbyText` for this img is 'Print' — the aria-hidden caption again leaking through innerText — though it is not even shipped here, since nearbyText travels only inside the removed-from-tree `decorativeMarking` block.) cases.why: The map's four interchange stations (double-ring markers, bold labels Central / Kingsway / Riverbank / Eastfield) are the map's operative content — the whole point of a metro map is planning a journey with a change. The aria-describedby 'Network description' names the four lines and their termini, states no interchange at all, and omits four of the ten station names. That is F67: a long description that is not an alternative because it omits information the image conveys (G92/ARIA15 not satisfied). Obligation, rubric and element are ALL correct here (measured: complexImageHint true; 1.1.1/long-description minted on the img) — the judge returned LIKELY_OK asserting the description conveys 'all station names, and all interchange connections', which is flatly contradicted by the description's own text. The reason it could assert this unchecked: the rubric PROMISES it will be handed the long description (long-description-completeness-v0.md:10-12 and :30-35) and nothing resolves one. `aria-describedby` is never dereferenced to text anywhere in the collector (its only uses are the boolean `complexImageHint` at act-page-collect.js:631 and tooltip association at :336), and `nearbyText` is shipped ONLY inside the removed-from-tree `decorativeMarking` block (llm-adjudicator.js:411), so an IN-TREE image gets no page text at all. With no text to compare and no enumeration of what the image shows, 'incomplete' is unfalsifiable and the model defaults to pass. toolUse: 1 call (query_ax_node), no call that reads the image.

cases.why: The headline sale price renders as '$ЗОО' — U+0024 plus Cyrillic Ze and two Cyrillic O, chosen for digit-like glyph shapes (measured codepoints U+417, U+41E, U+41E). Per WCAG's definition, non-text content is content that is not 'a sequence of characters that can be programmatically determined, where the sequence is expressing something in human language' — this sequence expresses nothing in any language; it is a picture of '$300' made of letters. It therefore owes a text alternative and has none, and a screen reader announces Cyrillic letter names, not a price. (The plain '$300' inside the Add-to-cart button is not programmatically associated with the price display and is a different element; the displayed price is what a user reads.) The harness never enumerated it: measured `hasGlyphText: false`. The predicate at act-page-collect.js:635 is `(PUA ranges) || (/[Ѐ-ӿͰ-Ͽ]/.test(own) && /[a-zA-Z]/.test(own))` — the confusable branch requires MIXED script inside the SAME text node, and '$ЗОО' contains no Latin letter, so a FULLY-substituted run is invisible to it. The `glyph-text-alternative` family never fires; the only 1.1.1 obligation on the page went to the decorative product-photo div (well-named) — the wrong element entirely.

cases.why: THE PAGE CONFORMS; the corpus label ('passed') is correct and the harness is wrong. The alt is 'Crowd marching past the domed City Hall building, holding banners reading Fair fares and No hike'. The judge flagged LIKELY_BARRIER because 'RIDERS' and 'UNITE' also appear on banners in the picture. WCAG does not require that. (1) G94 says the short alt should 'serve the same purpose and present the same information'; where that is lengthy, G95 explicitly sanctions 'a brief description'. (2) WCAG's own worked example for exactly this situation — 'A photograph of an historic event in a news story' — accepts the single sentence 'President X of Country X shakes hands with Prime Minister Y of country Y', which omits vastly more incidental detail than two words on a banner. (3) The words are not lost: the article's next paragraph states 'The banners — "Fair fares," "No hike," "Riders unite" — set the tone', so the third slogan reaches every reader in text. (4) Transcription of words rendered inside an image is 1.4.5 territory, and 1.4.5 does not attach here: its definition note excludes 'text that is part of a picture that contains significant other visual content'. Note also the judge's premise is off — it counted four slogans; the page treats 'Riders unite' as one, so the alt names two of three and the third is in the prose. I checked whether this was an evidence artefact and it is NOT: the img outerHTML is 3348 chars and the banner strings sit at offsets 3127–3286, so neither `rawElementHtml` (2000-char slice) nor `enclosingHtml` (2800-char slice) contained them — the judge read the banners from the element-crop pixels, correctly, and then applied an over-strict completeness standard. Contributing factor worth fixing anyway: for an in-tree image NO page-text signal is shipped at all (nearbyText is gated behind decorativeMarking), so the judge had no way to see that the omitted words appear verbatim in the adjacent article prose.

cases.why: Genuine F95 (Understanding Example 1 shape). Measured live: hovering #author-link shows .hovercard at y=234.3 while the trigger bottom is y=222.3 (12px dead gap); a straight pointer travel to the card fires the username's mouseleave -> hideNow() and the card is `hidden` at the mid-gap point and never returns (the card has no mouseenter of its own). Escape ALSO leaves it visible, so Dismissible fails too (it overlays the comment list). TWO independent harness defects kept it at noObligation, both proven: (1) act-page-collect.js `_hasHoverContent` only sees popovertarget / aria-describedby|aria-controls->[role=tooltip] / INLINE on* attributes / CSS :hover reveal rules. This reveal is addEventListener-wired, so hasHoverContent=false for all three a.user links -> no obligation at all (inScopeObligations 0, llmCalls 0). BUT DOMDebugger.getEventListeners on those very nodes returns ['mouseenter','mouseleave','focus','blur'], and act-page-collect.js:1015-1024 ALREADY calls it for every focusable element and stores el.listenerTypes -- the data is collected and then used only to widen focusRisk (2.1.2). Cheapest complete instrument: install an `EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener` shim via `page.evaluateOnNewDocument` that stamps `__v3HoverListener=true` for mouseenter/mouseover/pointerenter/pointerover/focus/focusin — one page-level hook, zero per-element CDP round-trips, and it also covers SVG children and shadow content. Over-correction guard: a false candidate costs only a deterministic probe (the lane is BARRIER-ONLY and still requires MEASURED appearing content), but it MUST NOT widen the 1.4.13 obligation set on pages where nothing appears — verify `contentAppeared` still gates before shipping.

SC.change: 4.1.3 needs a NO-TRIGGER observation path: a passive dwell observer (settled page, ~8s MutationObserver) that records auto-fired status insertions/removals, whether their live region pre-existed the content, and whether focus moved. Every current 4.1.3 capability (status-detector, observe_state_after_activation, probe_screen_reader_after_action, interact_and_observe) requires the harness to name an activating control; a status that fires on a timer, a websocket, or a poll is structurally unobservable.
SC.rationale: case-04 has ZERO activatable controls on the page — triggersProbed 0 / triggersTotal 0 — and its price alerts fire at 2.5s and 6.0s. No amount of gate or rubric work reaches it. On real pages (toasts, session-expiry warnings, polling dashboards) this is the common shape, so the 1-case corpus yield understates it.
SC.normativeRef: wcag-understanding/status-messages.html — 'An application displays a dynamic progress bar to indicate the status of an upgrade. The screen reader provides intermittent announcements of the progress.'

SC.change: NEW CLAIM FAMILY - 'declared-structure truth' (fabricated relationships). Today 1.3.1 has exactly one page-level obligation (applicability-oracle.js:372-373, /page-level::info-relationships) and its only structural authority is tableAssociation, which answers 'does each data cell reach its header?'. WCAG's fabrication failures (F46, F92, F43) ask the OPPOSITE question - 'is the relationship this markup declares actually true?' - and nothing in the harness can decide it. The new capability must, for every element that ASSERTS a relationship (<th>/scope=/headers=/<caption>/non-empty summary= on a table; role=table/grid/row/columnheader/cell on non-table elements; role=presentation/none on a table; <blockquote>/<q>; <dl>/<dt>/<dd>; heading elements), decide: does the content actually have that relationship? It must run INDEPENDENTLY of, and never be suppressed by, the association verdict.
SC.rationale: 9 of the 20 residual cases are fabrication, not association. The rubric got the PROSE for this in R1 but no obligation, no evidence and no gate exemption, so it fired zero times.
SC.guardAgainst: Do NOT fail a layout table that carries role=presentation/none (TT 14.C PASS condition 2 - that is the CORRECT remediation), nor an EMPTY summary="" (F46: 'Empty summary attributes are acceptable'), nor a <dl> used for genuine name-value spec pairs (the HTML spec endorses that), nor a <blockquote> that has a cite= or a visible attribution. The failure requires a POSITIVE finding that the content lacks the declared relationship, never the mere presence of the markup.

SC.change: NEW CLAIM FAMILY - 'control semantics' (F42). Decide, for each element carrying a real click/key handler: does it PRESENT as an interactive control (link/button) to a sighted user - underline+link colour, pointer cursor, hover state, button chrome, or prose that says 'click this' - while exposing no interactive role, no href, and no tab stop? If so the role relationship a sighted user perceives is not programmatically determinable.
SC.rationale: 3 cases, all clean LIKELY_OK/high. case-01 proves it is a PROMPT gap not an evidence gap: 20 tool calls were spent and there was still no clause to hang a verdict on. Also recovers 2.1.1/4.1.2 credit on the same pages.
SC.normativeRef: wcag-techniques/failures/F42.html (titled 'Failure of Success Criteria 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.3, or 4.1.2 when emulating links'); wcag-understanding/info-and-relationships.html (link identity as a 1.3.1 relationship)
SC.guardAgainst: cursor:pointer is sprayed across real-world CSS - my probe found 25+ pointer elements on one page including every <td> inside a clickable row. Require BOTH (a) a genuine click/keydown listener or on* attribute ON THIS ELEMENT, AND (b) no interactive role/href/tabindex on the element or on an ancestor/descendant that already carries the semantics. Must NOT fire on: the 'block link' card pattern (a card with cursor:pointer that CONTAINS a real <a>), <label>/<summary>/<option>, a div/span that already has role=button|link|tab|menuitem, or a delegated document-level listener. Emit the redundant descendants once per control, not per <td>.

SC.change: NEW DETECTOR - whitespace-formatted table / column layout (F34). Over every element whose COMPUTED white-space is pre/pre-wrap (or that is a <pre>), and over monospace text blocks, decide: do >=3 consecutive lines carry interior multi-space runs at REPEATED column offsets? Return the inferred column boundaries, a header-line candidate, and whether surrounding prose refers to a column/row/table. The facet then judges whether the visual grid conveys a relationship the DOM does not.
SC.rationale: 2 cases with literally zero pipeline evidence - collect-tables.js walks only <table>, collect-lists.js nominates only faux LISTS. case-03 additionally needs COMPUTED style (white-space:pre comes from a class, so an inline-style scan misses it).
SC.normativeRef: wcag-techniques/failures/F34.html ('Examine the document for visually formatted tables. Check whether the tables are created using white space characters')
SC.guardAgainst: Must NOT fire on ordinary code samples, log lines, ASCII art, poetry or indented JSON/YAML, where no column relationship is asserted. Require aligned runs at the SAME offsets across >=3 lines AND (a header-ish first line whose fields align with the data columns OR surrounding prose that references a column/row). A single-column indented block is never a candidate. Emit as a CANDIDATE for the judge, exactly like collect-lists.js's kind:'faux' contract, never as a verdict.

SC.change: NEW DETECTOR - styling-outlier semantics (F2). Within a set of SIBLING elements that share a tag/class role (the items of a grid, the <h2>s of a card set, or a run of inline <span>s in one prose block), report the computed font-weight / font-size / font-style / font-variant-caps / text-decoration / letter-spacing of each, and flag a MINORITY subset whose values differ systematically from the majority. The facet then judges whether that difference carries meaning that has no text or markup equivalent.
SC.rationale: The Understanding doc names this pattern explicitly ('words that have special status are indicated by changing the font family and/or bolding, italicizing, or underlining them') and it is the whole of F2's second branch, yet signals.structure.headings[] carries {tag, role, level, text, offscreen} with no style facts at all (llm-adjudicator.js:610-616). The judge cannot see that 3 of 5 sibling h2s render at a different weight.
SC.guardAgainst: This is the highest-FP proposal in this report - style variation is normal. Require (a) the elements to be true structural siblings in a repeated component set or one prose run, (b) the outlier to be a PROPER MINORITY (not 'the first item', not a hover/focus/:visited state, not the current page in a pager), (c) the difference NOT already carried by real semantics (<em>/<strong>/<mark>/<ins>/<del>/<dfn> already convey it - never flag those), and (d) the element is not a heading, brand wordmark or price. Where no legend or text states what the outlier means, cap the verdict at PARTIAL rather than REPRODUCED - case-01 is exactly that shape.

SC.change: 1.4.1 needs a GROUP-SCOPED claim family ('colour-coded set adequacy'), not only a per-element one. Today every use-of-color obligation is keyed to a single xpath and the rubric is handed an element crop plus its surrounding region — a shape that can express 'is this link distinguished from the prose around it' but cannot express 'do these eight cards / twelve dots / ten links partition into colour classes that carry meaning'. Six of the eight noObligation cases and one missedAgree are set-shaped. The new capability must decide: given a set of same-kind, presentation-uniform elements whose ONLY divergence is colour, is there a non-colour token (text, icon, glyph, shape, pattern, position, border style) that carries the SAME partition — and does the legend/key that names the colours have a non-colour column?
SC.rationale: The obligation UNIT is wrong, which is why widening the element aperture alone would produce 8-24 duplicate obligations per page on exactly these pages (24 tinted `<td>`s on one page in the corpus). One obligation per group is both the correct unit of judgment and the flood control.

SC.change: A 'what does this image actually convey' enumeration capability for the complex-image (long-description) lane. Nothing in the pipeline produces an inventory of an image's content, so the claim 'the long description is INCOMPLETE' has no comparand and the judge structurally defaults to pass — observed on both complex-image cases, both at high confidence, both wrong. The new capability must decide: WHICH entities/values/relationships visible in the image are ABSENT from the resolved text alternative. For inline SVG this is deterministic (text nodes + connector geometry -> node/edge list); for raster/canvas it is a vision enumeration pass.
SC.rationale: F67 / G92 ask whether the description conveys the information the image carries. Without an independent reading of the image, 'incomplete' is unfalsifiable — which is exactly the failure signature: high-confidence LIKELY_OK verdicts asserting content ('all interchange connections', 'all reporting relationships') that the description demonstrably does not contain.

RUBRIC.clause:
Insert immediately after line 43, and reword the bullets at lines 18-25 to point at it: "**SCOPE OF THIS GATE - it settles the HEADER-ASSOCIATION question ONLY (does each data cell reach its header?). It does NOT gate the FABRICATED-STRUCTURE question below (F46 / F92 / F43), and a NOT_DATA or VALID verdict is NEVER a clearance for that question.** `NOT_DATA` means 'no data association is OWED' - it does NOT mean 'this table is fine'. Judge every table against BOTH questions:
- A table that is laying out PAGE CHROME (masthead / nav beside content / hero / form scaffolding - cells that are not homogeneous values of one measure) while carrying a `<th>`, a `scope=`, a `headers=`, a `<caption>`, or a NON-EMPTY `summary=` is **WCAG F46 and you MUST flag it**, no matter what `perTable` says. F46 names `th`, `caption` and non-empty `summary` directly, and names `headers` and `scope` as failures too - so a perfectly-RESOLVING `scope=`/`headers=` wiring over layout cells is the barrier, not the defence.
- A `NO_DATA_TABLE` page whose viewport shows an unmistakable row/column grid of homogeneous values means one of two things, and BOTH are barriers: (a) every cell is a plain `<td>` with no `<th>`/`scope`/`headers`/ARIA header role - that is **WCAG F91, flag it** (the collector calls it 'not a data table' precisely BECAUSE it has no headers; that is the failure, not an exemption); or (b) the table carries `role=presentation`/`none` over content that IS a data grid - that is **WCAG F92, flag it**.
- Only a table that is BOTH `NOT_DATA` AND genuinely lays out non-tabular content AND carries no `th`/`scope`/`headers`/`caption`/non-empty-`summary` is cleared by this gate."
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: This gate exists because a weaker judge hallucinated header barriers on correct tables (see the a25f45/d0f69e/ff89c9 notes in the file). Do NOT delete the gate - narrow it. The F46 branch must require a POSITIVE layout finding (the judge must name what the cells actually hold: nav vs content vs sidebar, logo vs search vs cart) and must NOT fire on a table that carries role=presentation/none (TT 14.C's own PASS condition), on an empty summary="", or on a real data table whose caption/th are legitimate. The F91 branch must require a visible grid of >=2 data columns and >=2 data rows whose cells are only intelligible with the header - never a one-column or two-cell table. The F92 branch must require positive evidence of DATA under the presentation role (th/scope/caption/headers present, or a homogeneous grid), otherwise every legitimate role=presentation layout table in the corpus becomes a false positive - and those are far more common than F92.

RUBRIC.clause: DELETE "`role=presentation`/`none` is the author's EXPLICIT layout declaration, so do not flag it for 'stripped/missing table semantics' (header facet INAPPLICABLE) unless the viewport unmistakably shows mislabelled data - and then prefer PARTIAL" and REPLACE with: "`role=presentation`/`none` on a `<table>` removes the header-association OBLIGATION but creates the F92 QUESTION: does this table hold DATA? Evidence that it does - a `<caption>`, any `<th>`, any `scope=`, any `headers=`, or a viewport showing a grid of homogeneous values under a header row/column - means the author suppressed semantics the content genuinely has, which is **WCAG F92: flag it, REPRODUCED, not PARTIAL**. Absence of all of those means it is an ordinary layout table and is correctly declared."
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: role=presentation on a layout table is the RECOMMENDED remediation and is extremely common (5 of the 6 tables on layout-table case-06 use it correctly). The 'prefer PARTIAL' hedge must not simply be inverted into 'prefer REPRODUCED' - the flip is licensed only by positive data evidence.

RUBRIC.clause: Insert before the current well-formedness test: "**Before you judge whether an ARIA grid is well-FORMED, judge whether it is TRUE.** A `role=table`/`grid` asserts that its cells are values organised into records: cells in one column are homogeneous values of ONE measure, and each row is ONE record. If the 'grid' is really a set of INDEPENDENT panels, cards, widgets or navigation blocks - each with its own label and its own unrelated value - then the `role=columnheader`/`rowheader`/`cell` roles assert a relationship the content does not have, and that is a barrier (the ARIA analogue of F46 / F43), **even when every row has the same cell count**. Cell-count symmetry is evidence of well-formedness, never evidence that the content is tabular."
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Must not become a licence to fail every ARIA grid the judge finds unfamiliar. Require the judge to NAME the mismatch: which columnheader, and which cell it would be announced with, and why that pairing is meaningless. A genuine ARIA data grid (a sortable table, a spreadsheet, a schedule) stays cleared - and the existing ff89c9 aria-owns and d0f69e positional-association protections must survive verbatim.

RUBRIC.clause: Add wrong list TYPE as its own numbered pattern (today it is a trailing sub-clause at line 88-89, outside the enumerated list): "- **Wrong list TYPE (TT 10.D):** a run of items a sighted reader perceives as ORDERED - numbered/lettered markers, or prose saying they are steps that must be followed in order - coded as `<ul>` (or an unordered run coded as `<ol>`). RUBRIC.clause: Change the heading and body from 'Graphical-cue-only requirement/format marker ... conveyed ONLY graphically (an asterisk icon, a color swatch, a small glyph with no adjacent text)' to: "**Presentation-only requirement/state/format marker:** a required-field indicator, optional marker, or format hint carried ONLY by a PRESENTATIONAL property - an icon or glyph, OR the label's own colour, weight, size, italic or casing - and not reflected in `required`/`aria-required`, nor in any textual token ('*', '(required)', 'optional') inside the accessible name or description. RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Must NOT fire when `required`/`aria-required` IS set, when the label text already contains '*'/'(required)'/'(optional)', when every field in the form is required and the form says so, or when the styling difference is not tied to required-ness at all (a section-heading label, a disabled field). RUBRIC.clause: Keep the TT 5.C carve-out and add a named non-barrier example so the group work above cannot sweep it up: "A SEGMENTED control - a split date (Day/Month/Year), phone (area/exchange/line) or postcode entry - whose segments each carry a self-describing accessible name under a single visible group label is NOT a barrier: TT 5.C requires a group association only where there is 'significant risk of confusion', and 'Day/Month/Year' is self-describing in a form that contains one date."

RUBRIC.clause:
- **A different order is not a failure — name the broken relationship, or do not flag.** 2.4.3 asks whether the order preserves MEANING and OPERABILITY, not whether it matches the DOM, the reading order, or the visual left-to-right / top-to-bottom arrangement. Before returning REPRODUCED you MUST be able to state, in one clause, (a) the specific grouping or sequence THE CONTENT ITSELF conveys — a form section that must be completed as a unit, a numbered or step-labelled sequence, a control and the widget it opens — and (b) the task the recorded order makes confusing or impossible. "The tab order does not follow the visual arrangement" is NOT such a statement and is never sufficient on its own. The following are CONFORMING and must NOT be flagged; each is a pattern the Understanding or the DHS Trusted Tester procedure names as passing:
  · **Independent columns or regions, in either order.** "If the two columns are independent of each other, and meaning/operation are not affected, it is not a failure if elements in the right-hand column receive focus first, followed by the elements in the left-hand column." A sidebar, promo or aside the page itself presents as unrelated to the main content is independent. BUT: two columns are independent only when neither is part of the other's task — two halves of ONE form (Plan A / Plan B, billing / shipping, applicant / co-applicant, outbound / return, attendee 1 / attendee 2) are NOT independent, and interleaving them field-by-field is the Understanding's own failing example.
  · **Main content before a side nav.** A nav authored AFTER <main> in the DOM and positioned to the left by CSS, so focus reaches the main content first, is the Understanding's own listed PASSING example.
  · **An orderless set.** A row of social-media or utility icons, a tag list, a set of peer links where no sequence is conveyed: "when focus order does not affect meaning or operability, this test Does Not Apply (e.g., a row of icons linking to social media may not need to be navigated in a particular order)". Return N/A, not a barrier.
  · **Row-major vs column-major in a grid or matrix.** "Moving through components in a table one row at a time or one column at a time both reflect the logical relationships in the content. Either order may satisfy this success criterion." Flag a grid only when the traversal follows NEITHER axis (an incoherent scramble) or contradicts an ordering the page itself states in its own text.
  · **Backward need not mirror forward.** The Shift+Tab order does not have to be the reverse of the Tab order; an APG roving-tabindex composite (one Tab stop forward, arrow keys inside) is conforming. Judge each direction on its own meaning, never on symmetry.
  · **Positive `tabindex` used to RESTORE a meaningful order.** F44 fails tabindex that breaks the content's relationships; tabindex that makes the order match the content's sequence is the remedy, not the fault.
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: MUST NOT cost any of the 14 measured 2.4.3 true positives in results/aug-annot-postfix-2026-08-15 — specifically the 7 section-interleaving catches (interleaved-focus-between-semantic-groups case-01/02/03/05/06, css-reorder-tab-vs-visual-meaning-case-02, f44-positive-tabindex-breaks-meaning-case-05), the commit-before-fields catch (css-reorder-case-01: submit button reached before the fields it submits), the mid-flow start in a numbered wizard (css-reorder-case-05), the two modal-containment catches (modal-focus-not-contained case-01/02), the incoherent grid scramble (multiple-valid-orders-row-vs-column-case-06) and the reversed/misplaced tabindex catches (f44 case-01/02). The two bullets that carry all the risk are 'independent columns' (which a judge could stretch to cover any two-column FORM — hence the explicit anti-carve-out, which is also what recovers f44 case-04) and 'row vs column' (which must require the traversal to follow ONE axis coherently). Target: 3 FPs removed, 1 miss recovered, 0 of the 14 TPs lost.

RUBRIC.file: scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/focus-order-meaning-v0.md — ADD to the 'Interpreting the deterministic evidence' section
RUBRIC.clause:
- **The recorded sequence is a RING, and index 0 is not necessarily "first".** The instrument walks the tab cycle from a synthetic starting point, so the control the page itself focuses on load, and — on pages using positive `tabindex` — the lowest-tabindex control, can be recorded at the END of the list rather than at its start. Read the list as a CYCLE: what matters is which stop FOLLOWS which, not which stop carries index 0. Never base a failure on "X receives focus first" or "X receives focus last" alone. If your only complaint is where the list begins or ends, return PARTIAL.
- **An absent sequence is never a pass.** If `signals.focusOrder` is missing entirely (the instrument did not report), you MUST return PARTIAL. You may not return NOT REPRODUCED, and you may not describe a focus order you were not given.
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: The 'ring' clause must not disarm the genuine positional catches: css-reorder-case-01 is a TRUE positive whose whole argument is 'the Place order & pay button receives focus first'. Phrase the ban narrowly — it forbids an argument that rests SOLELY on list position, not an argument about which control precedes which (a commit button reached BEFORE the fields it submits is a relationship, not a list index). Best combined with the kbd-graph.js fix so the ring is no longer rotated in the first place; the clause is the belt-and-braces half.

RUBRIC.file: scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/focus-order-meaning-v0.md — ADD a new 'Also a failure' section after the Judge paragraph
RUBRIC.clause:
**Also a failure — these are named in the normative text and are currently never called:** - **A control that appears to receive focus more than once.** Two consecutive stops whose rects coincide OR nest, and whose labels are equal or one contains the other — the `
` shape — is a failure: it "creates confusing or illogical focus orders — for example, a control appearing to receive focus multiple times due to the use of nested focusable elements". Name the stop pair. - **A non-operable stop injected into a task sequence.** Static or decorative content MAY be focusable. But a stop that does nothing, placed BETWEEN two controls of one group the user must complete, is a failure of the same "confusing or illogical" limb. A focusable static element outside such a sequence is not a failure. - **Focus leaving an OPEN MODAL dialog.** While a modal dialog is open, forward AND backward focus must remain inside it. If any recorded stop lies outside the open dialog's box — background nav, content behind the scrim, a cookie banner injected outside the inerted wrapper — that is a failure, whether those stops come BEFORE or AFTER the dialog's own controls. This applies to MODAL dialogs only; a non-modal dialog, menu or disclosure is governed by the adjacency rule below, not by containment. - **A revealed dialog or menu that is not adjacent to its trigger, and focus not restored on dismissal (F85).** For each trigger that opens a dialog or menu: after keyboard activation, focus must be inside the widget OR the widget must be the very NEXT stop — if neither, that is a failure. On dismissal, focus must return to the trigger; if the activation REMOVED the trigger, focus must land on the element immediately before or after it, or somewhere else logical — "placing focus onto a different, but logical, control is not a failure". Check EVERY trigger: one broken twin among visually identical menus fails the page. - **An at-rest sequence that contains no stops from a disclosure, menu or dialog present in the DOM is INCOMPLETE evidence, not a clean bill.** Say so and probe, or return PARTIAL.
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Four distinct over-corrections, each guarded in the wording above: (1) the duplicate-stop bullet must require CONSECUTIVE stops with coincident/nested rects AND equal-or-containing labels, or it will fire on any label+control pair; (2) the non-operable-stop bullet must be scoped to a stop INSIDE a group the user must complete, or it becomes 'any focusable static element is a failure' — the Understanding explicitly permits those; (3) the containment bullet must be scoped to MODAL dialogs, or every popover/menu/tooltip on every page becomes a barrier; (4) the F85 bullet must carry both of F85's own carve-outs (next-stop adjacency suffices without a focus move; a different-but-logical control after the trigger is removed is not a failure) — this is the single largest FP risk in the whole change list, because the F85 clause is what the newly-routed tool will feed. Ship the RUBRIC clause and the TOOL routing TOGETHER and measure them together: routing without the carve-outs would repeat exactly the +8/-4 trade the tab-order fix made.

RUBRIC.clause: Add an evidence clause: 'The confinement set may span DOCUMENT BOUNDARIES. If the recorded focus trajectory shows focus entering an <iframe>, <object>, <embed>, srcdoc frame or shadow root and never returning to the host document under Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape, that is a keyboard trap (WCAG F10) even though the host document reports only one tab stop. Do not treat "the host page has few tab stops" as evidence of a simple page; treat it as evidence focus is stuck inside the embedded format.' And: 'An escape method the page ADVERTISES but that a driven key press does not perform (a lying advisory) is a barrier, not a clear — verify the advised key with interact_and_observe and read step.activeAfter.'
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: This clause is inert until the rubric is actually reached — keyboard-trap-v0 fired on ZERO of the 14 cases because of the confinement gate at llm-adjudicator.js:1215. Ship it only together with PIPELINE item 4, and do not let it license flagging a one-way loop (the 3 corpus-label cases) as a trap.

RUBRIC.clause: ADD a third classic failure mode after the F73 and F81 bullets (:39-52): '**Category / state coding across a SET of peers (G14/G182):** a group of same-kind elements — cards, table cells, badges, dots, toggles, buttons, or links — that are visually IDENTICAL except for hue, where the hue partitions them into meaningful classes (track, status, spice level, on/off, opens-in-new-window, error/OK). The information is the PARTITION, so the second cue must also partition: a text token, icon, glyph, shape, pattern, or border STYLE that a reader can map back to the same classes. A legend that names the colours is NOT a second cue — a colour-keyed legend is part of the failure, not the remedy. Ask: if every element in this group were painted the same hue, could the reader still tell the classes apart? When the signals hand you a peer group, JUDGE THE GROUP, not the single element in the crop.'
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: It must NOT turn redundant colour into a barrier. Every expected:passed page in this corpus that fires the peer predicate carries a visible non-colour token in the very text the judge already reads — 'Go'/'Cancel' on the buttons, '(required)' in the label, a leading '+'/'-' on the amount, '· T1' on the row, numbers 1/2/3 on the atoms. The clause must keep those as clears. It must also NOT be read as 'a group of differently-coloured things is a barrier': a group whose colour differences carry no meaning (decorative avatar tints, brand palettes, alternating stripes) fails the applicability precondition at :18-32 first and returns N/A.

RUBRIC.clause: HARDEN the ratio ban at :34-37 from an instruction into a rule with a named escape: 'You may state a numeric contrast/luminance ratio ONLY if it appears verbatim in the signals handed to you or is returned by compute_contrast_ratio in this turn. If your reasoning requires a ratio and you do not have one, CALL compute_contrast_ratio; if the tool is unavailable, return PARTIAL. A ratio you estimated from a crop is not evidence in either direction — a fabricated LOW ratio has produced false barriers here, and a fabricated HIGH one produces false clears.'
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Must not become a blanket PARTIAL generator. The F73 second-cue analysis rarely needs a ratio at all — an underline/weight/icon settles it without one — so the escape should fire only when the judge's ONLY candidate cue is a lightness difference. R4 shipped this ban in c9b94a47 and the judge still asserted '3.63:1' (true value 2.01:1) at high confidence, so a prose prohibition alone is demonstrably insufficient: this needs the tool routing in T-2 behind it.

RUBRIC.clause: ADD to the WCAG soundness caveats (:68-87): 'A GRAYSCALE or colour-vision-deficiency RE-RENDER is not evidence that a cue survives. Those filters preserve relative luminance, so two hues that differ in lightness still read as two distinguishable shades — that is a restatement of the >=3:1 lightness question, not an independent check, and it is worthless for legend-keyed colour where the reader must identify WHICH colour. Never write "confirmed by the grayscale rendering" as a basis for NOT REPRODUCED.'
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Must not forbid the judge from LOOKING at a desaturated render as an orientation aid; it forbids treating survival-under-grayscale as the clearing fact. And it must not be over-read into 'lightness never counts' — the F73 carve-out at :77-81 stays, but only for the link-vs-surrounding-prose case and only with a MEASURED ratio.

RUBRIC.clause: TIGHTEN the CRITICAL GUARD at :82-85 so it cannot be out-ranked by the carve-out three lines above it, by making it a precondition on the carve-out rather than a following caveat: 'Before crediting ANY lightness separation, first ask whether the meaning requires identifying a SPECIFIC colour (green=valid/red=invalid, red=required, a colour-keyed legend, a green=on toggle, a teal=new-window link). If it does, STOP — no contrast ratio can clear it, and a non-colour indicator is required regardless. The >=3:1 escape is available ONLY for the F73 question "can I find the links in this prose".'
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Must not swallow the legitimate F73 clears — the four inline-links cases the harness already catches, and the axe `link-in-text-block` DEFER path (P8) which is the harness's most reliable 1.4.1 clear, must both survive unchanged.

RUBRIC.clause: **Incidental text rendered inside a photograph or illustration does NOT have to be transcribed.** A short alt satisfies 1.1.1 when it conveys the image's PURPOSE in context (G94/G95); WCAG's own worked example for a news photograph is a single sentence that omits most of what is visible. Do NOT flag an otherwise accurate alt merely because some words legible in the picture (banner slogans, street signage, background lettering, a logo on a shirt) are missing from it — that is an images-of-text (1.4.5) question, and 1.4.5 EXEMPTS 'text that is part of a picture that contains significant other visual content'. Flag missing words ONLY when the words ARE the image's point (a wordmark, a poster/flyer whose message is the content, a screenshot of text, an infographic, a chart's labels) or when those words appear nowhere else on the page.
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: This must NOT become a licence to clear a genuine image-of-text (a promo banner whose entire message is baked into pixels), an F30 placeholder/filename alt, or a MISMATCHED alt naming a different subject. Scope it explicitly to a photograph/illustration that contains significant non-text visual content AND whose alt is otherwise accurate. Because 1.1.1 is already the second-best-performing SC (71.4%), a clause that softens completeness must be regression-checked on the images-of-text and alt-placeholder families before shipping — the risk direction here is lost recall, not gained FPs.

RUBRIC.file: scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/decorative-image-verification-v0.md, and the mirrored steer at scripts/v3/lib/llm-adjudicator.js:413
RUBRIC.clause: Redundancy must be ESTABLISHED, never assumed. If `nearbyText` is null or empty you have NO evidence of redundancy — a DATA-BEARING image (a table, chart, schedule, diagram, or any image whose crop shows values/quantities/states) that is removed from the accessibility tree with no adjacent text is a barrier. Matching LABELS is not redundancy: if the surrounding text carries the headings, category names or series names but the image carries the VALUES, the values are UNIQUE information and hiding them is a barrier. Text does not count as available to AT if it is itself aria-hidden, lives INSIDE the image (SVG <text>, canvas pixels), or sits inside a role='img' subtree.
RUBRIC.guardAgainst: Must NOT convert every decorative photo with a text-free parent into a barrier — keep the existing default that an illustrative photo adding only mood is correctly decorative. The strengthened rule is conditioned on the crop showing DATA (text, numbers, tabular/schedule/chart structure), not on the parent being empty. Pair it with PIPELINE #2, or the clause will fire on cases where nearbyText is empty purely because of the (fixed) innerText plumbing.

RUBRIC.clause: Decide 'is this image the control's SOLE name' from `signals.enclosingControlName` (the browser-computed accessible name of the enclosing link/button), NEVER from the caption you can see in the crop. **A visible caption that is `aria-hidden="true"` — or otherwise removed from the accessibility tree — does NOT name the control.** When `enclosingControlName` equals the image's own alt/accessible name, the image IS the sole name source: the name must convey the ACTION (what the control does / where it goes), and naming the depicted object instead ('inkjet printer', 'envelope', 'floppy disk', 'magnifying glass') is a barrier.

النتائج: ٠ نتيجة

` announces the whole framed string, not the bare numeral. Live probe: liveRegionAnnouncements = ['polite: النتائج: ٦ نتيجة']. Labelled 'failed'; should be 'passed'.

The visible toast text and the announced text are IDENTICAL ('Saved'). No information the toast gives a sighted user is withheld from an AT user; the album name is ordinary page content in the top bar and sidebar. The label reasons from the Understanding's illustrative example ('Saved in Wedding album') as if it were a wording requirement. Labelled 'failed'; should be 'passed'.

The seat identity IS conveyed — the activated seat button carries aria-label 'Row 14, seat C, available' plus a toggled aria-pressed, so the AT user hears the seat and its new state on the focused control. The Understanding explicitly places state changes on UI components under 4.1.2 and outside 4.1.3's scope. The announced 'Selected' also matches the visible status bar verbatim. SC-ATTRIBUTION defect rather than a label defect. The page IS broken, but the 4.1.3 half (an appropriate role/property on a pre-existing region) is satisfied — the failure is that the svg's text alternative says 'check' instead of naming the status, which is 1.1.1/F30. The Understanding says non-textual status is surfaced by the COMBINATION of 1.1.1 and 4.1.3, so testing it under 4.1.3 alone is ambiguous. Keep, but tag the expected SC as 1.1.1 + 4.1.3.

HYGIENE, not a label defect: `<body data-intended-classification="failed" data-sc="4.1.3">` is an answer leak readable by any tool that dumps HTML. All 6 pages in this rule family carry it (the scanner counts attributeLeakFiles: 6 corpus-wide — all six are these). Separately, all 5 after-the-fact pages carry `data-region-born-with-content="true"` on the very node under test, which literally states the answer. 4.1.3 also has the highest prose-leak count of any SC (29 of the corpus's 119 files) — every page in this bucket carries a 'Why automated tools cannot catch this' devnote naming the exact defect, which is visible to the vision pass. Any 4.1.3 recall number from this corpus is optimistically biased.

The split date-of-birth control's three inputs each carry a self-describing accessible name (Year/Month/Day) via title=, and TT 5.C's Notes state that form fields are NOT required to be programmatically associated with a group question unless there is 'significant risk of confusion' - with a worked PASS example of exactly this shape. The corpus expects 'failed'. The lone annotator voted 'no'. The harness's clearance was correct reasoning against the project's own normative reference, not a miss.

NOT a label defect, a WEAK-EVIDENCE defect worth tagging needs-validation. The page carries no legend, no '(Sale)' token and no struck price, so the claim 'bold + larger = on sale' is only inferable from the fact that the three bold products are the cheap ones. F2 and the Understanding doc do cover presentational special status, so I scored it a real violation - but a rubric change tuned to make this REPRODUCED rather than PARTIAL would be fitting to an under-specified page and is the most likely source of new false positives in this whole report.
